lineage_detail.description: Per-row provenance envelope. 'compact' (default) returns source_filing + source_url. 'full' adds accepted_at. 'off' omits lineage.

tools.name: get_institutional_holdings
tools.description: Returns top-N institutional holders of a US public company at a specific period_end (by default the latest period whose 45-day 13F filing window has closed), with aggregate institutional shares, total market value, holder count, and HHI concentration (sum of squared share-of-total percentages) over EVERY common-stock 13F holder of that period, not only the returned top-N rows.  Sourced from Form 13F-HR via the by-issuer partition.  Institutional plan only.  A newer quarter still inside its filing window is incomplete: it is skipped by default (named in newer_period_in_filing_window) and flagged by filing_window_open when requested explicitly.  staleness_warning fires when the latest data is older than 90 days.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol of the issuer — or a CIK (SEC identifier).

period_end.description: Quarter-end of the 13F reporting period (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit to use the latest period available. This is a REPORTING period, NOT a point-in-time cutoff — use as_of_date for that.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD): only 13F filings ACCEPTED by SEC on or before this date are considered, applied BEFORE the latest period is resolved. A 13F/A amendment or late filing accepted after this date is excluded (zero look-ahead) — use this for survivorship-free backtests. Omit for the latest knowable book.

top_n.description: Maximum holders to return, ranked by market_value_usd. Default 25, max 200.

include_superseded.description: Default false: 13F-HR rows replaced by a later 13F-HR/A are hidden once the amendment is knowable (as of as_of_date when given), so an original and its amendment are never both counted. Set true to include the superseded originals.

lineage_detail.description: Per-row provenance envelope. compact / full / off.

tools.name: get_manager_portfolio
tools.description: Returns a 13F filer's full portfolio at a specific period_end (latest by default), with QoQ deltas vs the prior quarter (new / increased / decreased / exited / unchanged).  Specify the filer either by filer_cik (preferred) or filer_name (fuzzy match against entity.name; multiple matches raise an ambiguity error so you can disambiguate by CIK).  Institutional plan only.

filer_cik.description: CIK of the 13F filer (1-10 digits; will be zero-padded to 10).  Preferred over filer_name when known.

filer_name.description: Filer name to fuzzy-match against entity.name.  Case-insensitive substring match.  Multiple matches raise INVALID_ARGUMENT — use filer_cik in that case.

period_end.description: Quarter-end (YYYY-MM-DD).  Omit to use latest available.  This is a REPORTING period, NOT a point-in-time cutoff — use as_of_date for that.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD): only 13F filings ACCEPTED by SEC on or before this date are considered, applied BEFORE the latest + prior periods (and the QoQ basis) are resolved. A 13F/A amendment or late filing accepted after this date is excluded (zero look-ahead). Omit for the latest knowable portfolio.

top_n.description: Maximum positions to return, ranked by market_value_usd. Default 25.

include_superseded.description: Default false: 13F-HR rows replaced by a later 13F-HR/A are hidden once the amendment is knowable (as of as_of_date when given), so an original and its amendment are never both counted. Set true to include the superseded originals.

tools.name: get_blockholders
tools.description: Returns SC 13D / SC 13G blockholder disclosures (5%+ stakes) for a US public company. Each row carries percent_owned, sole/shared voting + dispositive split, schedule_type, and the first-class ``going_active`` flag — TRUE when the same filer flipped 13G → 13D within the lookback window (the single most actionable activist signal in this dataset). Use latest_only=true (default) to dedupe to the most recent filing per filer.  Use collapse_groups=true to fold multi-person filings into one row. Institutional plan only.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol of the issuer — or a CIK (SEC identifier).

schedule_filter.description: Which schedule(s) to return.  '13D' = activist (intent to influence). '13G' = passive.  'both' = no filter.

as_of_date.description: PIT filter on accepted_at — only filings on or before this date.

latest_only.description: When true (default), keep only the most recent filing per (filer, schedule prefix) — typically what analysts want.  Set false to see the full filing history.

collapse_groups.description: When true, fold multi-reporting-person filings into a single row, with secondary persons in the ``persons[]`` field.  Default false: each person stays as its own row.

lookback_days.description: Window for the going_active (13G → 13D) detection. Default 365 days.

tools.name: get_insider_sentiment
tools.description: Role-weighted insider sentiment score on a fixed [-100, +100] scale for a single issuer over a lookback window.  Role weights: CEO/CFO = 3.0 (via officer_title pattern), other NEO Officer = 2.0, 10%-Owner = 1.5, Director = 1.0.  P = +1, S = -1; option exercises, grants, and tax withholdings are neutralised.  Cluster flag = TRUE when ≥3 distinct insiders transacted within any 30-day window inside the lookback. Institutional plan only.

ticker.description: Issuer ticker symbol — or a CIK (SEC identifier).

lookback_days.description: Days back from today to scan transactions for. Default 180.

cluster_window_days.description: Sliding window for the cluster_flag detection. Default 30 days.

tools.name: get_top_holders
tools.description: Classification-aware UNION across insider transactions (latest post_transaction_shares per insider), 13F institutional holdings, and SC 13D / 13G blockholder filings for one issuer.  Each row carries holder_class ∈ {insider, institutional, blockholder_13D, blockholder_13G}.  Dedupes overlapping filers by precedence (13D > 13G > institutional > insider).  One call, classified cap table — Bloomberg charges separately for INSIDER<GO>, OWNER<GO>, and HDS<GO>; this consolidates them.

ticker.description: Issuer ticker symbol — or a CIK (SEC identifier).

top_n.description: Maximum holders to return, ranked by shares. Default 25.

period_end.description: 13F REPORTING period_end. Omit for latest. NOT a point-in-time cutoff — use as_of_date.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD): only filings ACCEPTED by SEC on or before this date are considered across all three sources (institutional via accepted_at, insider via accepted_at, blockholders via accepted_at). Excludes amendments/late filings accepted after this date (zero look-ahead). Omit for the latest knowable cap table.

include_superseded.description: Default false: 13F-HR rows replaced by a later 13F-HR/A are hidden once the amendment is knowable (as of as_of_date when given), so an original and its amendment are never both counted. Set true to include the superseded originals.

tools.name: get_smart_money_flow
tools.description: Composite flow score on [-100, +100] aggregating insider transactions, 13F institutional Δ-shares vs the prior quarter, and SC 13D/13G blockholder changes over a lookback window. Each component normalised independently, then combined with configurable weights (default: institutional 0.4, blockholder 0.4, insider 0.2). Returns per-component attribution so an agent can see WHY the score is what it is — not just the headline number. NOTE: the institutional component is a QoQ share-change signal computed over the top-5 13F filers on a MATCHED current-vs-prior basis (a filer only counts when its prior-quarter book is observable), NOT the issuer's complete institutional book — treat the score as a directional signal, not an exact flow. `coverage.coverage_confidence` (0–1) reports how much of that basis had a real prior quarter; when it is 0 the institutional component is forced to 0 so a 13F ingestion gap can never surface as a false max-conviction buy. See the `coverage` block for holder coverage + staleness. The score is a unitless composite, not a dollar figure. Institutional plan only.

ticker.description: Issuer ticker symbol — or a CIK (SEC identifier).

lookback_days.description: Lookback window for insider + blockholder components. Default 90.

weight_institutional.description: Weight applied to the institutional component (0–1).

weight_blockholder.description: Weight applied to the blockholder component (0–1).

weight_insider.description: Weight applied to the insider component (0–1).

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD) applied to all three legs (institutional, insider, blockholder) via SEC accepted_at — filings accepted after this date are excluded so the composite is computed with zero look-ahead. Omit for the latest knowable signal.

tools.name: get_ownership_pack
tools.description: Who owns the company and who is moving, in ONE call, already cited: top holders (13F, insiders, 13D/13G), recent insider transactions and insider sentiment, blockholders including 13G to 13D flips (`going_active`), and the smart-money flow composite. Each section is the underlying tool's output unchanged (quote `metrics_display` verbatim). A section that fails carries its own `status` and error and sets `degraded: true`; it is never shown as empty. Point-in-time: `as_of_date` is passed to every section; insider sentiment has no as-of date, so it is not run in a dated case (`status: not_point_in_time`, which does not set `degraded`). Institutional plan (the smart-money tools' gate); below it the pack returns the plan refusal with its upgrade options.

ticker.description: Company ticker or CIK (SEC identifier), e.g. 'AAPL' or '0000320193'. A CIK is the stable identifier.

lookback_days.description: Window for insider transactions and flow. Default 180. Ignored for insiders when `as_of_date` is set.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cutoff: every section reads only what the SEC had accepted by this date. A section that cannot honour it is not run and says so.

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: Fetch the current HEAD of a report by id. `format=markdown` returns the rendered body, `format=json` returns the full structured payload (sections + citations + report-type-specific data), `format=preview` returns abstract-only. Authors see any of their own reports; non-authors only get `preview` of listed reports and need the report's required tier for full bodies. A guest who is not the author always gets the preview, whatever `format` asks for. For an archived prior version use `get_report_version`, not this tool.

tools.name: search_reports
tools.description: Search the catalog of published research reports. All listings are free to read. Filters: free-text (matches title + abstract), ticker, report_type. Sort: `newest` (default) or `oldest`. Tier-gated: callers only see reports their plan tier can read.

ticker.description: Filter to a single subject ticker.

price_max_cents.description: Reserved for future paid listings; currently ignored (all reports are free).

cursor.description: `next_cursor` from the previous page; omit for the first page.

tools.name: compute_dcf
tools.description: Forward discounted-cash-flow valuation (two-stage Gordon-growth model) under YOUR assumptions: you give stage-1 growth, WACC, terminal growth and horizon; it returns the per-share intrinsic value (`value_per_share_cents`, cents of `result.reporting_currency`, never converted) and a 5×5 WACC × terminal-growth sensitivity grid. Valuein publishes no precomputed DCF, DDM or fair value: this tool is the only intrinsic value, and it is a scenario under the stated assumptions: a different discount rate is a different answer, so where it matters run more than one set of assumptions and give the range. In prose quote `result.metrics_display` verbatim (e.g. "$249.17"; each grid cell carries `value_per_share_display`), never the cents, and state the assumptions beside it. Inputs pulled from the filings (any can be overridden): FCF base = operating_cash_flow − capex; net_debt = total_debt − (cash + short-term investments), with `result.net_debt_basis` saying whether it was reported or cash was assumed zero; a debt is never assumed: with no total debt in the facts (`net_debt_basis: "debt_not_reported"`) the value per share, equity value and grid are null with a `reason` and only the enterprise value is returned; shares = CommonSharesOutstanding, else net_income / eps_diluted (`result.shares_source`; both are cited, and the implied count is part of the id). Use the returned net debt, shares and bridge; never recompute them. `result.inputs_echo` and `result.inputs_provenance` cite each input's `fact_id` (the FCF base carries a `derived_id`). When every input came from cited facts (fcf_source "trend", no override) `result.outputs_provenance.value_per_share.derived_id` (and `terminal_value_pct`, `enterprise_value`, `equity_value`) and each grid cell's `derived_id` encode your assumptions so the arithmetic can be re-derived: cite them beside the figure. An override, a three_statement run or a degenerate model ships no id: quote those as your own assumptions. A null `value_per_share_cents` (WACC ≤ terminal growth, FCF base ≤ 0, or a missing input) is NOT a zero valuation; `reason` explains. Optional `share_price` (a price the user gave, with its date) adds `result.upside_pct`. `fcf_source: "three_statement"` feeds the linked projection of `project_three_statement` into the same PV math (`stage1_growth_rate` then ignored; detail in `three_statement_detail`). Persists nothing: use `create_report` (report_type 'reverse_dcf') to save. A bank (its operating cash flow is deposits and lending, not free cash) is refused with METHOD_NOT_APPLICABLE and `extensions.see_instead`: no value, whatever the inputs. Plan: Benchmark and above.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol of the company to value, e.g. AAPL, MSFT, BRK.B.

stage1_years.description: Number of explicit high-growth projection years before the terminal stage (3–15). Defaults to 5.

fcf_base_override.description: Override the auto-pulled FCF base (USD). Leave unset to use R2-derived.

shares_override.description: Override shares outstanding. Leave unset to use R2-derived.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD) for the auto-pulled inputs. Fundamentals are filtered by SEC accepted_at (strict PIT). Omit to use the latest knowable inputs.

share_price.description: Optional share price YOU supply (never from memory) for the company valued, same fields as a `compute_price_multiples` row (cik optional, ticker not used). Adds `result.upside_pct`: the DCF value per share against your price, with the price and its date in the figure's `derived_id`. Call it your price, user-supplied, with its date.

cik.description: SEC Central Index Key of the company. Preferred over a ticker.

price_date.description: Date the close belongs to, YYYY-MM-DD. Required: a price without a date is refused.

close.description: Closing price per share, in `currency`: above 0, at most 10,000,000, at most 8 decimal places.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of the close, e.g. USD.

adjustment.description: How the close was adjusted; default raw. split_adjusted needs adjusted_through. total_return is refused for multiples.

adjusted_through.description: For split_adjusted: the date the adjustment runs to (YYYY-MM-DD).

source_label.description: Your own note on where the price came from, at most 64 characters. Shown as yours.

as_of.description: When the price was observed, ISO 8601 with offset. Default: 16:00 America/New_York on price_date.

fx_rate.description: Units of the company's reporting currency per 1 unit of `currency`; needed when the currencies differ. Also yours.

fcf_source.description: "trend" (default): compound fcf_base by stage1_growth_rate every year (unchanged original behavior). "three_statement": derive the FCF stream from a full linked 3-statement projection instead — see the tool description for details.

three_statement_assumptions.description: Only used when fcf_source is "three_statement". Overrides for the underlying projection; unset fields use project_three_statement's defaults.

tools.name: forensic_audit
tools.description:
Deterministic forensic-accounting scores for a single ticker: partial Beneish M-Score, Sloan accruals, and a solvency snapshot. Returns a red-flag narrative ranked by severity, with citations to source filings. Used by the `forensic_earnings_brief` SOP.

Note: full Beneish needs AR / current assets / PPE / SGA / current liabilities, which aren't in our fundamentals model. We compute the recoverable subset (SGI + TATA + LVGI) and flag `partial=true`. For a bank the M-Score, its components and Sloan accruals are null (`null_reasons`: NOT_MEANINGFUL_FOR_SECTOR); the solvency snapshot is still served, its debt ratios with a `sector_notes` sentence (borrowings only, deposits excluded). Plan: Benchmark and above.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol of the company to audit, e.g. AAPL, MSFT, BRK.B.

tools.name: get_pit_valuation_ratios
tools.description: Point-in-time trailing-twelve-month (TTM) financials for a company on a historical date, safe for backtesting: every figure comes from SEC filings accepted on or before `as_of_date`, so no later information leaks in. TTM sums the four most recent standalone quarters (or uses the latest fiscal-year filing when no quarterly series exists). Returns TTM revenue, gross_profit, operating_income, EBITDA, net_income, OCF, CapEx, FCF; a balance-sheet snapshot (diluted shares, cash, debt, net debt, book equity); and TTM gross, operating and net margins. No share price and no price-based multiple is returned: for a multiple on a price the user gave you, use `compute_price_multiples`; for the price-free reference values (graham_number, ncav_per_share) use `get_valuation_metrics`. Use for historical fundamentals screens, backtest entry-point financials and peak/trough forensics. Plan: Pro (most recent 15 years) or Institutional (back to 1993); on a free plan it returns ENTITLEMENT_DENIED before any read.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL, MSFT — or a CIK (SEC identifier), e.g. '0000320193'.

as_of_date.description: The historical date for the snapshot (YYYY-MM-DD). Only filings accepted on or before this date are read. Use a recent date for the latest figures, or any date back to 1993 (subject to your plan's history window) for the figures as they were observable then.

tools.name: run_backtest
tools.description: A SMALL, BOUNDED, in-Worker sanity-check backtest — NOT a full-universe backtesting engine. Answers a quick question like 'does this factor actually work on these 5 names over the last year' inline, mid-conversation, without leaving MCP. Composes two existing tools (`get_pit_universe` + `get_pit_valuation_ratios`) across up to 10 tickers x 12 rebalance dates (120 cells): for each rebalance date, checks which requested tickers were in the survivorship-free PIT universe on that date (dropping — never erroring on — a ticker not yet listed or already delisted), then pulls each surviving ticker's point-in-time TTM margins. Returns a flat {rebalance_date, ticker, factor_values, next_rebalance_date, next_factor_values} grid (FILINGS ONLY: no returns are computed, the tool takes no price input; `next_factor_values` is what the next filings showed, the same margins point-in-time on the following rebalance date, so 'did margins hold after this date' reads straight off the grid; see `prices_note` in the response) — a quick cross-sectional factor snapshot, NOT a transaction-cost-aware portfolio simulation or a statistically validated backtest result. If the requested grid exceeds 120 cells, this tool does NOT silently truncate — it returns a `stream_fallback` response (signed Parquet download URLs, same shape as `get_compute_ready_stream`) and tells you to use those URLs. For a REAL full-universe, multi-date, survivorship-free backtest, use the Python SDK's AlphaEngine (`pip install valuein-sdk`) looped over `as_of` dates client-side — this tool is explicitly the small complement to that, not a replacement for it. Pro and Institutional only: it composes get_pit_valuation_ratios (TTM financials), which needs the Pro plan, so the free plans receive an ENTITLEMENT_DENIED upgrade envelope before any read. Coverage follows your plan tier same as the two tools it composes.

rebalance_dates.description: 1-12 historical dates (YYYY-MM-DD) to snapshot TTM margins on. Order does not matter — the tool sorts them chronologically. Each cell also reports the factors as the NEXT date in the sorted list shows them (filings only, no returns).

factors.description: Which of get_pit_valuation_ratios's own output fields to include as factor_values. One or more of: gross_margin_pct, operating_margin_pct, net_margin_pct. Omit to include all of them.

tools.name: project_three_statement
tools.description: Linked forward Income Statement / Balance Sheet / Cash Flow projection, seeded from the company's latest historical annual period. The balance sheet ties out (assets == liabilities + equity) EVERY projected year by algebraic construction — each year's `tie_out_ok` field is a live correctness check, not decoration. Interest is computed on beginning-of-period debt balances (no circular cash-sweep/revolver solve — deterministic by design). Gross margin, operating margin, and the combined D&A + working-capital adjustment are held at the seed period's ratio-of-revenue unless overridden; interest_rate_on_debt and tax_rate are ASSUMPTIONS (no historical InterestExpense concept exists in the dataset). Every simplification is listed in the response `caveats[]` — read them before presenting this as a precise forecast. Returns a `fcf_stream` usable directly as `compute_dcf`'s `fcf_source:"three_statement"` input. Plan: Benchmark and above.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL, MSFT, BRK.B.

years.description: Projection horizon in years (1-15). Defaults to 5.

revenue_growth_rate.description: Flat annual revenue growth rate applied every year (e.g. 0.08 = 8%/yr).

interest_rate_on_debt.description: Annual interest rate on beginning-of-period debt. Assumption — default 0.06.

tax_rate.description: Effective tax rate on positive pretax income. Default 0.21 (US statutory).

gross_margin_pct_override.description: Override the seed period's gross margin (held flat across all years). Leave unset to use the historical ratio.

operating_margin_pct_override.description: Override the seed period's operating margin. Leave unset to use the historical ratio.

capex_pct_of_revenue_override.description: Override the seed period's capex-as-%-of-revenue ratio. Leave unset to use the historical ratio.

cash_sweep_pct.description: Fraction (0-1) of each year's free cash flow swept to debt paydown. Default 0 (going-concern; use ~1.0 for an LBO-style paydown).

dividend_payout_pct.description: Fraction (0-1) of net income paid out as dividends each year. Default 0.

new_debt_draw_year1.description: New debt drawn at year 1 only (absolute USD) — e.g. acquisition financing. Default 0.

new_equity_draw_year1.description: New equity contributed at year 1 only (absolute USD) — hits cash + equity symmetrically. Default 0.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD) for the seed period. Omit to use the latest knowable annual period.

tools.name: compute_lbo
tools.description: Leveraged buyout returns analysis: caller provides entry/exit multiples, leverage, and a hold period; the tool builds a Day-1 pro-forma opening balance sheet from the deal's own sources & uses (cash-free, debt-free convention — entry_debt = leverage_multiple x EBITDA, sponsor_equity = entry_enterprise_value + minimum_cash - entry_debt), then runs it through the same linked three-statement engine as `project_three_statement` (100% FCF-to-debt-paydown sweep by default). Returns MOIC and IRR (solved by bounded bisection over the sponsor's cash flow stream — interim dividends if any, plus exit equity proceeds). EBITDA is PROXIED by operating income (no separate D&A concept exists in the dataset) unless entry_ebitda_override is supplied — see `result.entry_ebitda_is_proxy`. `result.irr.converged:false` means no root was found (e.g. a total wipeout) — never a fabricated rate. Every simplification is listed in `result.caveats[]`. A bank is refused with METHOD_NOT_APPLICABLE and `extensions.see_instead`: an LBO of a deposit-funded balance sheet means nothing. Plan: Benchmark and above.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol of the LBO target, e.g. AAPL.

exit_multiple.description: EV/EBITDA multiple assumed at exit. Defaults to entry_multiple (no multiple expansion/contraction) when omitted.

hold_period_years.description: Hold period in years (1-10). Defaults to 5.

revenue_growth_rate.description: Flat annual revenue growth rate applied every year of the hold (e.g. 0.05 = 5%/yr).

interest_rate_on_debt.description: Annual interest rate on beginning-of-period LBO debt. Default 0.08 (leveraged debt typically prices above IG).

tax_rate.description: Effective tax rate on positive pretax income. Default 0.21.

cash_sweep_pct.description: Fraction (0-1) of each year's FCF swept to debt paydown. Default 1.0 (standard LBO — 100% sweep).

dividend_payout_pct.description: Fraction (0-1) of net income distributed to the sponsor each year (dividend recap style). Default 0 — most LBOs return capital only at exit.

minimum_cash.description: Minimum operating cash left on the pro-forma opening balance sheet. Default 0.

entry_ebitda_override.description: Override the EBITDA figure used for both entry and exit multiples. Without this, EBITDA is proxied by operating income.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD) for the seed period. Omit to use the latest knowable annual period.

tools.name: compute_accretion_dilution
tools.description: M&A accretion/dilution: the standard sell-side/banker quick-screen for whether a proposed acquisition adds to (accretive) or subtracts from (dilutive) the acquirer's EPS in the first pro-forma year. Pulls net income + shares outstanding for both companies. A share price comes from `get_price_history` (a graded daily close, cited with its date and grade) or from the user, never from memory: for a stock deal (cash_pct < 1) pass the acquirer's share price as acquirer_share_price_override (a user's price is called user-supplied); the target's price only discloses the offer premium. Caller sets the consideration mix (cash_pct, cash-financed by new debt or the acquirer's balance sheet), annual run-rate synergies, and the new-debt interest rate. A SINGLE pro-forma-year bridge — NOT a multi-year merger model; synergy ramp, integration costs, and purchase-price-allocation amortization (goodwill/intangibles step-up) are not modeled (see `result.caveats[]`). `result.accretion_dilution_pct` positive = accretive, negative = dilutive. Plan: Benchmark and above.

acquirer_ticker.description: Acquirer's stock ticker symbol, e.g. MSFT.

target_ticker.description: Target's stock ticker symbol, e.g. ATVI.

cash_pct.description: Fraction (0-1) of deal value paid in cash; the remainder (1 - cash_pct) is paid in acquirer stock.

synergies_pretax.description: Pretax annual run-rate cost/revenue synergies (USD). Default 0.

cash_financing_source.description: Where the cash consideration is funded from. "new_debt" (default) applies an after-tax interest drag; "balance_sheet_cash" applies none.

new_debt_interest_rate.description: Annual interest rate on new acquisition debt (only used when cash_financing_source is "new_debt"). Default 0.06.

tax_rate.description: Effective tax rate applied to synergies and the interest drag. Default 0.21.

acquirer_share_price_override.description: The acquirer's share price in USD, supplied by you. Required when cash_pct < 1.

target_share_price_override.description: The target's share price in USD, supplied by you (used only for the disclosed premium). Leave unset to skip the premium.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD) for both companies' fundamentals. Omit to use the latest knowable data.

tools.name: compute_price_multiples
tools.description: Market cap, P/E, P/B, P/S, EV/EBITDA, EV/revenue and dividend yield on a share price you pass (1 to 25 per call), joined to point-in-time SEC EDGAR filings. Pass a price only from `get_price_history` (a graded daily close; put its `close_source` and grade in `source_label`), or one the user gave you or a tool the user connected returned in this conversation; never from memory. Each row needs the price date, the close, its currency and (for the record) where it came from in `source_label`, e.g. the `get_price_history` source, your market-data provider, broker export or internal price database. RULES: a price joins only filings accepted BEFORE it was observed (default 16:00 New York on `price_date`); a ticker means the company that held it ON `price_date`; splits effective after the filing and on or before the price date are applied to the filed share count and per-share figures, and a split between period end and filing is not (the filing already holds it); a company with more than one listed share class gets no multiple at all (`multi_class_price_needed`); a price in another currency needs `fx_rate`; a `total_return` close is refused; a `split_adjusted` close needs `adjusted_through`. OUTPUT per price: `metrics`, `metrics_display` (QUOTE VERBATIM), `metrics_provenance` (each figure's `derived_id`, the filed `fact_id`s behind it and `rests_on: ["user_supplied_price"]`), `metrics_unavailable` (why a figure is null), `warnings`, and `price_inputs_echo` (the price exactly as you sent it, `basis: "user_supplied"`). When you write a figure that rests on a price, state the price, its date and its source beside the figure (a user's price is called user-supplied; a `get_price_history` close is cited with its grade and IEX or SEC attribution); cite the `derived_id` so `verify_facts` can re-run it. The price is never called current. Check that your price and the filing use the same share basis; a split missing from the corporate-action table is not detected. Nothing is stored. Use `as_of_date` to cap the filings used. Plan: every plan, including no sign-in.

cik.description: SEC Central Index Key of the company. Preferred over a ticker.

ticker.description: Ticker, resolved to the company that held it ON price_date (recycled tickers map by date).

price_date.description: Date the close belongs to, YYYY-MM-DD. Required: a price without a date is refused.

close.description: Closing price per share, in `currency`: above 0, at most 10,000,000, at most 8 decimal places.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of the close, e.g. USD.

adjustment.description: How the close was adjusted; default raw. split_adjusted needs adjusted_through. total_return is refused for multiples.

adjusted_through.description: For split_adjusted: the date the adjustment runs to (YYYY-MM-DD).

source_label.description: Your own note on where the price came from, at most 64 characters. Shown as yours.

as_of.description: When the price was observed, ISO 8601 with offset. Default: 16:00 America/New_York on price_date.

fx_rate.description: Units of the company's reporting currency per 1 unit of `currency`; needed when the currencies differ. Also yours.

prices.description: 1 to 25 prices, one per company and date.

as_of_date.description: Optional cap, YYYY-MM-DD: only filings accepted before the end of this day are used, even when a price is later.

tools.name: list_report_versions
tools.description: Author-only newest-first listing of a report's archived version history. Each entry summarises what changed (sections edited, etc.) so the workspace UI can render a clickable history without loading every artifact. Pair with `get_report_version` to fetch a specific version's content for diffing against HEAD. Any plan; only the report's author gets rows.

report_id.description: Identifier of the report whose version history to list, as returned by create_report or list_my_reports.

limit.description: Maximum number of archived versions to return (1–100). Defaults to 20.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous response's `next_cursor` — the smallest version number on the previous page. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: get_report_version
tools.description: Author-only fetch of a specific archived version of one of your reports, by positive-integer `version`. Returns metadata + the full payload (sections, citations, structured, markdown) — enough to render a diff against the current HEAD in the workspace editor. Use after `list_report_versions` identifies the version number you want; for the current HEAD use `get_report` instead. Any plan; only the report's author gets rows.

report_id.description: Identifier of the report whose archived version to fetch, as returned by create_report or list_my_reports.

tools.name: render_report
tools.description:
Return a 15-minute presigned download URL for a report in the requested binary format.

`format=md` presigns the cached markdown — instant, no compute. `format=docx` and `format=pdf` return the SAME branded research-note design in the two media: a masthead-first page 1 (Valuein letterhead — brand rule, wordmark, 'EQUITY RESEARCH' kicker + date), the ticker eyebrow and title, the named analyst's byline, then the body (abstract, sections with full markdown incl. GFM tables, citations table with clickable SEC EDGAR links) and a running footer (ticker, 'Built on Valuein · valuein.biz', page N of M, one disclosure line). The PDF embeds the Geist brand faces with figures set in tabular mono. `format=xlsx` returns an Excel workbook of the report: a Report sheet (one row per block, with its block id) and a Citations sheet (each claim with its fact ids, filing accession, form, period and EDGAR link), so every figure keeps its source. Binary renders are cached in R2 after first build so repeat downloads are instant; pass `force_regenerate: true` to bust the cache (e.g. right after `update_report`).

Tier gate mirrors `get_report`: authors always see their own reports; non-authors below the report's required tier get an upgrade prompt.

format.description: md = raw markdown (the same body the editor renders). docx = branded Word document; pdf = the same branded research-note design as a shareable PDF (Geist faces embedded, clickable citation links); xlsx = Excel workbook with a Report sheet (every block, with its block id) and a Citations sheet (claim, fact ids, accession, form, period, EDGAR link), so each figure keeps its source.

force_regenerate.description: If true, ignore the cached DOCX/PDF and re-render. No effect on md (markdown is canonical).

author_name.description: Display name of the report's author, shown as a named byline ('By {name}') on the masthead — the way a real research note credits an analyst. Omit to show 'Valuein Research'. Only affects the binary formats; ignored on a cache hit (the cached file keeps whatever byline was baked in on first render — pass `force_regenerate: true` to refresh it).

tools.name: generate_dcf_xlsx
tools.description:
Render a forward DCF result into a professional Excel workbook (Summary + 5×5 Sensitivity heatmap + Inputs sheet). Native conditional formatting — no chart images needed. Returns a 15-minute presigned R2 download URL.

SERVER-TRUST: the DCF is re-derived in-Worker from the supplied `inputs_echo` (the math is pure + deterministic) and the workbook renders Valuein's recomputed figures — never the caller's claimed values. If the claimed figures disagree, the workbook is still produced but stamped with a visible correction banner and the response `verification.status` is 'corrected'. A fabricated per-share value can never appear as Valuein-authoritative.

Pair with `compute_dcf` for a typical analyst flow: agent calls `compute_dcf({ticker, ...})`, then passes the structured result straight to `generate_dcf_xlsx({ticker, dcf_result, ...})` to materialise a shareable file.

Plan: Pro and above.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol of the company the DCF workbook is built for, e.g. AAPL.

company_name.description: Optional — surfaces on the cover row. Falls back to ticker only.

dcf_result.description: Structured DCF result — typically the `result` field returned by `compute_dcf`.

tools.name: generate_research_brief_docx
tools.description:
Render a structured research brief into a professionally-styled Word document — a branded masthead-first page (Valuein letterhead: brand rule, wordmark, 'EQUITY RESEARCH' kicker + date, then the ticker eyebrow, the title as hero, and the named analyst's byline), the body (abstract, optional snapshot table with figures in mono, markdown sections incl.
